Yandex Games quickstart for Yes2SDK, followed by the moderation requirements a Yandex submission has to satisfy.

Make your games run everywhere people already are, no web build required # Yes2SDK for Yandex Games - Platform Guide
## Prerequisite
- **Unity:** UPM git URL https://github.com/yes2games/yes2sdk-unity.git#, then Yes2SDK > Build Window > Install Template.
- **Defold:** add the release archive to game.project \[project\] dependencies, then Project > Fetch Libraries ## Requirements
Yandex Games has specific SDK integration requirements for game approval ### API Requirements
The Yes2SDK methods below cover every Yandex-platform call you need. | Platform Requirement | Yes2SDK API | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| YaGames.init() → ysdk | Yes2SDK.initializeAsync() | Required |
| ysdk.features.LoadingAPI.ready() | Yes2SDK.startGameAsync() | Required (otherwise loading screen never dismisses) |
| ysdk.features.GameplayAPI.start() | game.gameplayStart() | Required (analytics + ad timing) |
| ysdk.features.GameplayAPI.stop() | game.gameplayStop() | Required (before every ad) |
| ysdk.on('game\_api\_pause', ...) / 'game\_api\_resume' | Yes2SDK.on('pause', fn) / on('resume', fn) | Required (mute audio during ads) |
| ysdk.on(EVENTS.ACCOUNT\_SELECTION\_DIALOG\_OPENED, ...) / ...\_CLOSED | Yes2SDK.on('accountDialogOpen', fn) / on('accountDialogClose', fn) | Optional (pause while the account switcher is open) |
| ysdk.adv.showFullscreenAdv({ callbacks }) | ads.showInterstitial(placement, cbs) | Recommended |
| ysdk.adv.showRewardedVideo({ callbacks }) | ads.showRewarded(placement, cbs) | Recommended |
| ysdk.adv.showBannerAdv() | ads.showBanner('bottom') | Optional (sticky banner revenue) |
| ysdk.environment.i18n.lang | session.getLocale() | Recommended (multi-language) |
| ysdk.getPlayer() | player.getPlayer() (pre-loaded on init) | Optional |
| player.getData() / setData() (cloud) | data.getInt/setInt, data.getString/setString, ... | Optional (auto-syncs to cloud) |
| ysdk.auth.openAuthDialog() | auth.signInAsync() | Optional (cloud data without auth = device-local) | ## How to Submit
1. Build your game (Unity WebGL or Defold HTML5) and zip the output
2. Upload the zip on your game page (**Onboarding → Stage 1**)
3. Fill in title, description, icon, and screenshots on the **Game Profile** stage (**Onboarding → Stage 2**). Yandex requires all of these
4. Test the build in the Inspector (**Onboarding → Stage 3**)
5. Click **Request Publish** in **Onboarding → Stage 4** and select Yandex ## Yandex-Specific Notes
### Sticky Banners
- Yandex supports sticky banners at the bottom of the screen
- Call Yes2SDK.ads.showBanner("bottom") to enable
- Revenue is additional to interstitial/rewarded ads ## Common Issues
### Game loads slowly on Yandex
Yandex wraps your game in an iframe with additional SDK overhead. Keep your build size under 15MB for best experience ## Build & Upload Limits
- **External requests:** external hosts must be whitelisted in console; https/wss only
- **Compression:** Brotli/Gzip with Decompression Fallback ENABLED (cannot set Content-Encoding on Yandex hosting), or Disabled

By default, Yandex Advertising Network (YAN) monetization must be enabled in the game. If you do not want to monetize your game, then in the console on the **Draft** tab in the **Developer’s comment** field, directly state your decision.

  - **Interstitial blocks**: ad blocks that completely cover the app background and show up at certain points (for example, when accessing the next game level). *Important: Mute sounds before showing the ad!* ## 🌒 Lua API
### 🌒 ADVERTISEMENT (docs)
#### yagames.adv\_show\_rewarded\_video(callbacks)
- rewarded function - Called when a video ad impression is counted. Use this function to specify a reward for viewing the video ad (e.g., add coins, unlock features). **The rewarded callback is called before close, and you should update your in-game UI only after close.** ### 🌒 ADVERTISEMENT - STICKY BANNERS (docs)

local yagames = require("yagames.yagames")

end)

I'm thinking through the design for a game I'm calling «РОЙ» (The Swarm) — it's a Vampire Survivors-like where you control an auto-attacking entity that grows in size, with a Russian-language theme and one-button controls.

The core mechanic is that you're a single cell in a primordial ocean, enemies are hostile organisms, XP are food pellets, and leveling up triggers evolution. I'm mapping out the full design doc now to keep scope tight while making it feel polished. The game has a title screen with meta progression (spending biomass on permanent upgrades like speed, HP, magnetism, and damage), then runs through a 15-minute campaign with waves every minute, elite enemies every 3 minutes, and bosses at 3 and 6 minutes. Weapons and evolutions unlock as you level, with a run summary screen at the end showing stats and offering an ad-revive option. The weapon progression is what drives the addictive moment-to-moment decisions.

I'm laying out the starting weapons: a basic spike that fires at the nearest enemy, a passive orbiting body that damages on contact, an expanding shockwave that slows, a bouncing projectile, and a short-lived swarm burst every 8 seconds. Then there are higher-tier evolutions that combine weapons with passive items—like the spike evolving into a homing needle burst when paired with speed, or the orbit evolving into a larger rotating shield with knockback.

I'm also defining passive upgrades like movement speed, max health with healing, damage multiplier, cooldown reduction, projectile count, and XP magnetism, with each stat capped at 5 levels.

For enemies, I'm setting up chasers that move directly at you, fast erratic darters, splitting blobs that divide into smaller pieces, shooters that fire projectiles, and larger tank enemies.

The real retention hooks are the dopamine of constant level-ups with a shrinking XP bar, the strategic tension of picking the right build at each level, the escalating visual and audio intensity, and the permanent meta progression that makes you stronger each run so you always want to try again.

I'm also factoring in the daily reset bonuses for a 2× first run, ad placements that reward players without forcing them, leaderboards for competitive play, and achievements that unlock new characters. I want to layer in haptic feedback through canvas shake, hitstop on impact, and particle effects to make everything feel snappy and responsive.

Now I'm structuring the codebase...

Setting up the project files... For Yandex's review, the loading screen needs to hide the ad after it finishes. # РОЙ (Swarm) — design & retention rationale

A **reverse-bullet-hell / auto-battler survivor** ("Vampire Survivors" loop) for Яндекс Игры.
Single HTML5 build, no image/audio assets, zero dependencies. Playable at `index.html`.

## Why this shape, on this platform

The concept was chosen against Yandex's own 2025 data ([App2Top interview with Nikita Bokarev](https://app2top.ru/2025-in-video-games/summarno-opublikovali-24-ty-syach-igr-a-snyali-29-ty-syach-nikita-bokarev-iz-yandeks-igry-ob-itogah-2025-goda-237710.html)):

- **Midcore is now top-5 on the platform** and average session time is approaching **~60 min**. A survivor loop is the canonical "one more run" midcore shape: trivial to start, deep enough to hold long sessions.
- **Hybrid monetization (ads + IAP) is the stated standard.** This loop is built around it: rewarded revives, rewarded double-biomass, optional interstitial between runs, and an IAP-shaped meta currency.
- **Quality bar rose** (catalog cut from ~29k to ~19k). A survivor with a real meta-progression layer and polished juice is exactly the tier they now promote; a bare clicker is not.

## The retention loops (why people don't bail)

1. **Micro (seconds):** constant levelling. XP curve starts ~7-10 per level so the first level-up lands in ~12s and cadence eases smoothly. Every kill drops a magnetised gem, every level a choice. This is the dopamine engine.
2. **Meso (one run):** build-making. Three-offer choices, weapon + passive synergies, and an **evolution** as the mid-run payoff. Evolutions are deliberately *guaranteed a slot* once reachable and the HUD shows a live goal tracker ("Иглы 1→6 + Рефлекс 0→3") so the player always has a visible target — the "one more level" pull.
3. **Macro (between runs):** biomass meta-currency spent on permanent upgrades, unlockable characters gated by achievements, daily bonus, and offline earnings. This converts every death into forward progress, so quitting never feels like loss.

## Verified, not assumed

Everything below was executed in a real headless Chromium against the actual build (see `tools/playtest.mjs`), with per-system frame attribution (`tools/fixed.mjs`, `tools/rprof.mjs`):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Boot, menu, all screens, help | ✓ |
| Full run to game-over | ✓ level 17-23, ~3.5 min |
| Level cadence | first level ~12s, smooth ramp |
| Evolution reachable in a normal run | ✓ at level ~12 (was 29 before fix) |
| Rewarded-ad revive path | ✓ |
| Persistence across reload | ✓ |
| Meta upgrade purchase | ✓ |
| WASD + touch input | ✓ |
| Console errors | 0 |
| Sim cost @ 230 enemies | ~0.6-0.9 ms/tick |
| Render @ 1.7MP, 220 on-screen enemies + traps | ~10-21 ms (software rasteriser; far faster on GPU) |

### Bugs found & fixed by the test (real retention bugs)
- Level-up panel never closed → game unplayable past level 1.
- Evolutions RNG-hidden → the payoff was never seen; now guaranteed + surfaced.
- Full-screen gradient fills every frame → 4-6x frame cost; now pre-rendered.
- Animated `setLineDash` traps → ~0.2ms each; replaced with a cheap mesh.
- Menu-state render crash (null player) → uncaught error every frame.

## Monetisation wiring (Yandex-compliant)
- Rewarded buttons state the ad + exact reward (rule 1.5) and are optional.
- Audio muted + gameplay stopped before every ad (rule 1.7); `game_api_pause`/`resume` handled.
- Interstitials throttled ≥60s, never on run 1.
- `YaGames.init` → `LoadingAPI.ready`, `GameplayAPI.start/stop`, player cloud save, leaderboards — all with graceful local fallback so it runs outside Yandex too.

## Where to go next
- Real art pass + character skins (IAP), more characters/evolutions (content treadmill),
  daily challenges, weekly leaderboard resets, push-style return hooks via daily bonus.
